facts.fact: Tom Allen was seriously ill in early 1903, confined to his bed for weeks with persistent colds at his home on Market Street, and his manager Don Murphy said he would soon be out again.
facts.conflict: onset: at Christmas (198.c1) vs confined by 31 January (194.c1, 195.c1) vs took to his bed about late February (203.c16)

facts.fact: Tom Allen planned to marry his nurse and housekeeper, Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove of St. Louis, once he recovered, on his birthday, 23 April 1903.
facts.conflict: age of Mrs. Hartgrove: 21 (197.c2, 1000.c1) vs 31 (201.c2); Allen's birthday: his 65th (1000.c1) vs his 64th (201.c2)

facts.fact: Tom Allen was taken to the Baptist Hospital at Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, on 28 March 1903, after the physician diagnosed pneumonia and advised removal; he was seriously ill there.
facts.conflict: date of removal: Friday 27 March (1004.c7) vs Saturday 28 March (198.c4, 198.c5)

facts.fact: Allen's daughter, Mrs. Mary Taylor, went to the Baptist Hospital on 30 March 1903 with Robert Lyons and was refused admittance, having been told her father was too ill to talk to anyone after the report of his engagement.
Mrs. Taylor said her mother and sister were living in Birmingham, England.
Tom Allen died at the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, early on Sunday 5 April 1903, at the age of 6-, and his body lay at an undertaking establishment.
facts.conflict: date: 5 April (most claims) vs 6 April (262.c16, a 1978 retrospective article). cause: general debility (206.c1) vs pneumonia diagnosed on 28 March (198.c4). 262.c16 says he was still operating Sportsmen's Rest, while other claims name his place Champions' Rest.

facts.fact: Some retrospective articles placed Tom Allen's death in St. Louis in 1904 or 1905.
facts.conflict: year: 1904 (240.c3, 252.c4, 253.c12, 247.c1, which gives 5 April 1904), about 1905 (221.c4, 242.c12) vs 1903 in the contemporary reports (253.c12 notes that other articles give 1903)

facts.fact: Tom Allen was buried in St. Louis on Wednesday 8 April 1903, after a funeral from an undertaking establishment, with pallbearers including former prize fighters, his daughter standing by the coffin with her four children, and the funeral procession going to the cemetery.
facts.conflict: start: expected from his home over No. 615 Market Street (203.c3) vs from Wand's undertaking (204.c4), Farley & Wand at 211 South Sixth Street (207.c3). pallbearers: Chris Lauff, J. Fletcher, Tom Kelly, Andy Kirk, Tom O'Donnell, Gus Ellis (207.c4) vs Charlie Daly, Chris Lauff, Jack Fletcher, Tom Kelly, T. Neusel, Tom O'Donnell, Gus Ellis (208.c4). daughter named Polly Taylor (204.c4, 207.c5) vs Mary Taylor (198.c3, 202.c10). Mrs. Hartgrove and the daughter stood on opposite sides of the bier (204.c4).
